Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:45 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (CTO - Celestia), Amy Zhou (Head ML), Luis Alvarez (Infra), Rachel Park (Compliance), Tom (PM)
summary: Redwood walkthrough of the Model Catalog focused on selecting open models, benchmark profiles, and the compatibility matrix for private/dedicated deployments. Customer is evaluating options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC) for a HIPAA-sensitive clinical summarization product. Key outcomes: agree to run a pilot benchmark with Celestia prompts; Redwood to share security docs and pricing; plan infra deep-dive to scope VPC/private deploy and GPU compatibility.
topics: Model catalog filters and curated open models
Benchmarks (latency/throughput/cost) and how to read performance profiles
Compatibility matrix: quantization, CUDA/cuDNN, GPU families, sequence length tradeoffs
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for HIPAA workloads
Batching, KV cache and prefix caching effects on cost/latency
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and this is Priya, our solutions engineer. We're gonna walk through the model catalog and then show how benchmarks and compatibility matrix help pick a model for Celestia's use case.
[00:08] Mark: Hey Jordan, thanks, excited. Quick note - Rachel's on for compliance questions. We're mostly focused on on-prem or VPC options but want to see hosted first.
[00:15] Priya: Great, we'll start high-level then dive into the console and the model catalog. Quick clarification - are you planning to run clinical summarization, is that the primary workload?
[00:22] Amy: Yeah summarization + some entity extraction, and we also need embeddings for semantic search. Latency target is sub-400ms p95 for single-turn summarizations, cost is also a factor.
[00:33] Luis: From infra side we run on AWS today, mixed C5/G4 instances, but willing to look at Dedicated GPU pools; also curious about CUDA versions and NVLink compatibility.
[00:41] Jordan: Perfect. So first slide - model catalog is a curated list of open and validated models, we show perf profiles, token costs and a compatibility matrix. (link: drive.redwood/model-catalog-deck)
[00:52] Priya: Jumping into the console - you can filter by task (summarization, embeddings), model family (Llama-2, Mistral, Falcon), size, and quantization compatibility. Note: our corpus of benchmarks includes both latency and throughput for common sequence lengths.
[01:08] Tom: Quick question, how do you represent sequence-length effects? We have long clinical notes sometimes 2-3k tokens.
[01:14] Priya: We run benchmarks at multiple seq lengths - 512, 1024, 2048 - and show kernel-level perf. For long sequences we recommend models with better KV cache efficiency; the catalog marks those.
[01:24] Mark: Are those benchmarks run on naked GPUs or with your runtime (i.e., Redwood runtime)?
[01:28] Priya: Good question. Each benchmark row notes the environment: hosted-prod (Redwood runtime on A100s), dedicated (customer-dedicated pools), and an approximation for ONNX/torchscript for local infra. Sometimes the notes get noisy - e.g., "A100 80GB, batch=1, seq=512". We include [throughput, latency p50/p95], and cost-per-token estimated.
[01:44] Amy: How do you handle quantization? If we go 4-bit quant, how much quality hit do we expect for summarization?
[01:49] Priya: We publish quantization profiles per model: accuracy delta on our eval sets (ROUGE/BLEU-ish for summarization, and embedding cosine for vector tasks). For many Llama-2 variants 4-bit QAT is acceptable, but for instruction-heavy summarization we recommend 8-bit or mixed precision to preserve quality. There's also our Optimize tool that suggests quant/bs/batch configs.
[02:05] Luis: Compatibility matrix - what columns are there? CUDA version? cuBLAS? Triton?
[02:10] Priya: The matrix includes: model architecture, recommended kernel (fused attention / flash-attn), supported quant formats (4-bit/8-bit), tested CUDA versions, GPU families (A100, H100, L4, RTX 6000), and notes on multi-node KV sync. It's not perfect - occasionally the model label in the matrix is slightly off (transcription: "Falcon forty B" labelled as "Falcon 40b-oo") but we keep it updated.
[02:27] Rachel: For HIPAA we need KMS, audit logs, and private networking. Do you have example architecture diagrams?
[02:33] Jordan: Yes - we'll send the SOC2 + architecture + KMS/HSM integration docs after. For Private we offer a control plane that can be in customer VPC, and you can run inference in your own infra with our runtime container.
[02:44] Mark: For the pilot can we test with our prompts and realistic traffic shape? Also want to simulate cold vs warm cache.
[02:50] Priya: Absolutely, pilot plan is typical: provide sample prompts, we'll run hosted and dedicated runs, collect p50/p95 and throughput, and simulate prefix caching differences. We'll instrument cost per 1M tokens and projected monthly spend.
[03:03] [03:03] Speaker 1: (mumbled) so are you able to fallback if a model is down?
[03:07] Priya: Yes - smart routing and fallback policies: route by latency, cost, or region; automatic fallback to a compatible variant (e.g., Llama-2-13b -> Llama-2-7b) if needed.
[03:14] Amy: Does the catalog expose evals? Like you can see a model's rouge on our medical summarization eval?
[03:18] Priya: We surface both generic evals and allow customers to upload their eval sets; Optimize ties regression alerts back to prompt sets so you can detect quality drops when changing quant or model.
[03:27] Jordan: Demo time - console view: top-level table shows model, size, task, latency p95, tokens/sec. Click into a model shows compatibility matrix and a "Benchmarks" tab.
[03:38] [03:38] Priya: (screen) Here's Llama-2-13B fine-tuned variants: note perf on A100 vs H100, 4-bit vs 8-bit. Also see a note: "embedding dims and batch shapes impact memory for KV cache".
[03:51] Luis: On memory - if we use 2k seq and batch 4, would 13B fit on 80GB?
[03:56] Priya: Typically yes for 13B with 8-bit; 4-bit helps more. But for 2k*4 you need to watch KV scratch; that's in the compatibility notes. We can run an exact sim for your payload during the pilot.
[04:07] Mark: Any third-party benchmarking? We've seen different numbers from Benchy folks.
[04:11] Priya: We publish both internal and community benchmarks and encourage customers to run their own. The catalog has a "benchmark provenance" column.
[04:18] Amy: What about embeddings - we need high accuracy at reasonable cost for semantic search across EMR notes. Which models do you recommend?
[04:24] Priya: For embeddings we surface dedicated models - smaller embed-specific models are often more cost-effective (e.g., Mistral-embed variants or optimized Llama embeddings). We include cosine similarity on our medical embedding eval sets.
[04:34] Jordan: I'll flag that for the pilot to include embedding quality targets and recall at K metrics.
[04:39] Rachel: For compliance, will audit logs include token-level redaction or PII filters?
[04:43] Jordan: We can redact at ingestion or keep a configurable retention policy; we offer audit logs and can support minimal retention for PHI. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[04:52] Tom: Pricing - do you have a chart showing hosted unit cost vs dedicated reserved capacity?
[04:56] Jordan: Yes; hosted is pay-as-you-go per token with usage rates that vary by model/size. Dedicated is a reserved capacity with commitments; we show projected unit costs per token based on utilization. The Optimize tool helps compute the sweet spot (batching, caching, quantization) to reduce unit cost.
[05:12] Priya: One more thing on the compatibility matrix - we also mark models that support kernels like cutlass/fused-attention which reduce latency for long sequences; those kernels sometimes require specific CUDA/toolkit versions. So infra compatibility matters.
[05:26] Luis: That answers my CUDA question; we'll need a clear matrix for our infra team.
[05:30] Jordan: We'll send the GPU compatibility spreadsheet. Also note that for Dedicated we can provision L4s for cheaper embedding workloads if that fits.
[05:38] Amy: Any caveats with instruction tuning or RLHF variants? Sometimes they behave differently under quantization.
[05:44] Priya: Exactly - RLHF/instruction-tuned models can be more sensitive. The catalog flags which checkpoints were used for eval. For those we recommend validation on your prompt set before committing to aggressive quant.
[05:57] [06:00] (screen) Priya: Showing "Compatibility" tab for a Mistral derivative - see rows for tested CUDA 11.8, 12.1 and notes about kernel fallback.
[06:11] Mark: Good. For rollout strategies: can Redwood do canary deploys or AB tests between models?
[06:16] Jordan: Yes - Console supports rollouts with canary % split, automatic fallback, and we track per-route metrics (latency, cost, error rates). We also tie rollouts to quality gates.
[06:26] Amy: We need regression alerts for key prompts - is that in Optimize?
[06:29] Priya: Yup, Optimize supports prompt-set based regression detection and will alert if metrics drop beyond thresholds.
[06:35] Luis: For the pilot - what's the timeline?
[06:37] Jordan: Typical pilot is 2 weeks of benchmarking + a week for infra setup if Private. We can start hosted benchmarks within days.
[06:44] Jordan: Ok quick recap of next steps - Jordan will send security docs and pricing, Priya will share the GPU compatibility/benchmark spreadsheet and pilot plan, Amy will share sample prompt sets and traffic shape.
[06:53] Mark: Sounds good. Also please include a suggested model shortlist for our use case.
[06:58] Priya: We'll propose 3 model choices: a high-quality 13B instruction-tuned (Llama-2-13B variant), a cost-optimized 7B with 4-bit where acceptable, and an embeddings-specialized model for semantic search.
[07:11] Rachel: We'll review SOC2 docs and follow up with legal if needed.
[07:15] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
[07:19] Amy: Thanks.
[07:20] [END]
